title: Instruments and resolution worksheet with answers
subject: Science
unit: Summer 1: Review of Key Stage 3 and working scientifically (9C)
source: Seeded from science/y9 lesson 47 (Instruments and resolution worksheet with answers (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 47: Measuring: resolution, accuracy and precision. To understand how the choice of instrument and method affects the quality of measurements

questions.q: A 10 ml measuring cylinder or a 100 ml one for measuring 8 ml? Why?
questions.model: Smaller cylinders have smaller divisions, so better resolution for small volumes. 8 ml fits in 10 ml: choose it.

questions.a: Read with the eye level with the scale

questions.q: For six measurements on the sheet, choose the best instrument and resolution and give a reason.
questions.a: Sensible choices (as on the answer sheet), e.g. thickness of paper: micrometer or measure 100 sheets with a ruler
questions.model: Teacher does the first: 'mass of a coin: a balance reading to 0.01 g, because a coin is only a few grams'.

questions.q: Measure the thickness of one sheet of paper by measuring 100 sheets. Explain why this is more accurate.
questions.a: e.g. 100 sheets = 10 mm, so one = 0.1 mm; the ruler error is shared

questions.q: Why can a stopwatch reading to 0.01 s still give imprecise results?
questions.a: Human reaction time (about 0.2 s) is much larger than the resolution

questions.q: Big question: which flour reading is right, and does it matter?
questions.a: The balance has finer resolution; it matters only if the job needs that exactness.
